claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by formation of a stable oxide layer.
Annealing above 1000°C promotes formation of a stable oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu.
The stable oxide layer acts as a barrier to mechanical wear.
The stable oxide layer acts as a barrier to corrosion.
Oxide-layer barrier action reduces the coating's wear rate.
An annealed FeNiCrCoCu coating will have better wear resistance and a lower wear rate than an as-deposited coating.
The proposed mechanism applies from 1000°C to 1200°C.
The proposed mechanism applies under loads from 10 N to 100 N.
A controlled testing atmosphere will minimize oxidation during high-temperature wear testing.
Failure of the annealed coating to exhibit a significantly lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is intended to promote oxide formation, while the wear-test atmosphere is intended to minimize oxidation. These can coexist only if the oxide is preformed and retained during testing, but the annealing atmosphere and oxide-retention requirement are not specified.
